decision: NO-GO for H3 as preregistered; programme pivots to new preregistered questions
summary: No candidate met a preregistered stop rule, so no test partition was opened. On the primary family a 5-seed population GRU ensemble (tune NLL 0.7102) beat the best personalisation candidate (F3, 0.7237; +0.0135 [+0.0082, +0.0183]); with matched ensembles the candidate's gain shrank to -0.0014 [-0.0048, +0.0019]. Explicit personalisation added at most 0.009 nats/choice to a single model on single-session tasks, within seed noise. Earlier-session history is worth +0.0145 to +0.0195 when in-context state is lost between sessions (external GBE data) - the pivot question. All numbers exploratory (tune partitions).

A.note: own-history adaptation beats a donor's (exploratory); A1 not run; no joint freeze

B.note: B1 nominal tune pass vs a biased single-seed twin; B2 fails on the primary family (-0.0034 vs 0.005 margin)

C.note: best candidate behind or level with the strongest comparator in every counted family (tune)

D.note: cross-family pretraining helps at k = 16 but the meta-learned candidate is no better than plain pretraining

E.note: F4 earns the most reward but shows no savings on return to a seen context (development seeds)

F.note: observed happiness ratings worsen choice prediction slightly: +0.0010 [+0.0005, +0.0015], n = 9,413

G.note: requires an ethically reviewed prospective randomised study

evidence_level: exploratory (tune partitions / development seeds); critic recomputed central contrasts
